how: Use the onboard blood pressure cuff on a supported arm.
Measure after a few minutes at rest, restrained or seated.
Record the top (systolic) number in mmHg.

why.text: Weightlessness changes the heart and blood vessels, potentially increasing the risk of cardiovascular events.

if_abnormal.now: Check the cuff size and position. If the crewmember is unresponsive, start the CPR protocol.
if_abnormal.remeasure: Measure again after the crewmember has rested, with the same device.
if_abnormal.tell_ground: Add the readings to the next ground report.

space_note: After landing, Apollo crews' average standing systolic pressure was 13 mmHg lower than before flight (118.8 to 105.8). Safety bound: systolic below 90 mmHg, an Earth reference, no space data (AHA 2020); no upper limit sourced.
labels: Earth reference, no space data (Safety bound)
